text:
maria: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel-selection change I'm seeing a regression on Mixtral-MoE serving in prod. p50 up ~8ms and p99 up ~45ms. Not all routes affected.
ashok: which kernel change? the one that prefers fused attention kernels when seq_len < 1024?
maria: yep, landed --kernel=autoselect switch in runtime 2.7.2. Regression shows up on Mixtral routes using top-k=2 router and heavy prompt prefix reuse.
devin: any profiling data yet?
maria: small flamegraph from prod tracer attached below (snip). main hotspot is `dispatch_expert_kv` and `router_scatter` on GPU.
perf-bot: [profile] job=moe-router-174 -> attach: /artifacts/moe/profile-175030.log
kevin: can you paste the p99 latency histogram and the kv cache hit rate?
maria: p50 28ms -> 36ms, p95 120ms -> 160ms, p99 420ms -> 465ms. Expert KV cache hit rate dropped from 91% -> 73% for some customers.
sylvie: that KV hit drop suggests cache eviction pressure due to expert parallelism change? We recently increased experts-per-device in the dedicated pools.
ashok: we also changed kernel selection order: prefer cuBLAS for small GEMMs, fall back to custom kernels for MoE scatter. Seems scatter perf is worse in that path.
ashok: i'm attaching the small profiler snippet:
```
GPU time breakdown:
 - router_logits: 6.4ms
 - topk_select: 2.1ms
 - dispatch_expert_kv: 14.7ms  <-- increased
 - expert_compute: 24.0ms
 - gather_replies: 9.2ms
```
maria: dispatch_expert_kv is the new hotspot. Also noticed increased PCIe copies between host and device for KV shards.
kevin: are we hitting the expert cache pressure metric? what does `expert_cache_bytes` look like?
maria: yes — `expert_cache_bytes` spiked and we saw extra evictions. Configs: top_k=2, expert_capacity=1024 (per-expert), experts_per_gpu=16 -> increased to 20 last week.
devin: hypothesis: more experts per GPU -> smaller per-expert cache -> higher eviction -> more mem copies to refill -> dispatch overhead + kernel path chosen exacerbates it.
sylvie: can we try reverting kernel-selection priority on a canary and keep expert-parallelism as-is to isolate?
maria: I spun up a canary with `--kernel-prefer=custom_scatter` on two nodes (canary-23). Early numbers: p99 reduced ~20ms vs canary-with-autoselect. Cache hit rate recovered ~6 points.
ashok: good. Also want to test adjusting `router_logits_temp` and top-k routing to see if we can reduce router churn: maybe top_k=1 for high-throughput routes and increase expert_capacity.
kevin: what about RoPE scaling impacts? Mixtral uses RoPE scaling in some variants — could different token window cause kernel selection to switch because sequence length distribution changed?
devin: yes, if average seq_len increases past kernel threshold (1024) autoselect picks different GEMM tiling which may not be optimized for sparse dispatch. We saw that with Qwen tests last quarter.
maria: for immediate mitigation, can we: 1) pin kernel to custom_scatter on Mixtral MoE 2) bump expert_capacity to 1536 for affected pools 3) run router top-k=1 A/B for high-traffic routes?
ops-bot: rollout request created: ROLLOUT-1128 (pin-kernel). Canary target: eng-runtime-canary-3, 2 nodes.
sylvie: +1. Also add a sampling profiler (every 10s) on canary to capture router imbalance metrics.
kevin: i'll prepare a kernel microbenchmark harness to compare fused vs custom scatter for dispatch sizes (batch*topk) = [64,128,256,512]. Will post numbers.
devin: add kv-cache eviction traces to the logs (eviction_id, victim_expert, reason). That will help correlate.
maria: thanks — i'll keep the thread updated. If canary stabilizes we can promote the pin and then iterate on better kernel heuristics (maybe a runtime cost model that factors in expert_cache_hit_rate) :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Deployed config change (canary) at 1750301402 by maria — flags: kernel=custom_scatter, expert_capacity=1536
perf-bot: Canary initial metrics (10m): p50 30ms, p95 130ms, p99 440ms -> p99 improved vs baseline canary (autoselect) by ~18ms. Expert cache hit rate -> 80%
maria: early signs look promising. We'll keep sampling for another 2 hours before wider rollout.
kevin: after microbenchmarks i'll open a tracking issue for smarter kernel selection and add cost heuristics (include expert cache hit, seq_len dist, dispatch size).
nashok: note for the issue: also evaluate RoPE scaling variants; we saw small perf cliffs when head_dim changes and GEMM shape becomes unfriendly.
sylvie: thanks all. If anyone sees other Mixtral regressions tag this thread.
maria: closing loop for now — will update when we have final canary pass. :sparkles:
